newsitem.title: GREECE: Minor clash marks Athens Polytechnic march.
newsitem.headline: Minor clash marks Athens Polytechnic march.

text.p: Greek police put down violence by anarchist youths on the anniversary of a 1973 student revolt against the military junta of the day, but authorities said the Sunday march was the most peaceful for years.
"There were some small incidents but everything went well. It was the calmest (anniversary) in years," Public Order Minister Goerge Romeos told reporters.

Riot police threw percussion bombs at a group of about 70 stone-hurling youths, dispersing them minutes after they started fires near Athens Polytechnic, where a revolt against the junta which ruled from 1967 to 1974 was crushed with tanks.
Police said earlier they had used tear gas.

The clash followed an annual memorial march through Athens which ended peacefully. The November 17 march is usually uneventful but young anarchists often rampage through central Athens after it is over.
Some youths tried to enter the school but were thwarted by polytechnic guards without police intervention, police said.
Shortly before the incident, a gas-bomb attack against the State Scholarship Foundation in the Plaka area of Athens damaged the door of the building, he said.
A group called "Children of November" claimed responsibility for the attack and police said it was probably an attempt by anarchists to draw police away from the Polytechnic.

About 5,000 demonstrators earlier marched through Athens to the American embassy to commemorate the bloody uprising which helped bring down the U.S.-backed dictatorship. At least 20 students died but many historians put the number much higher.

Police on hand to prevent possible violence outnumbered the demonstrators by around three to one. They said the unusually large number around the capital was meant to head off any attemps by rioting youths to take over Athens Polytechnic.
After last year's march, hundreds of youths describing themselves as anarchists occupied the school, set fire to it and caused considerable damage.
Police arrested 470 youths after two days of clashes and more than 100 were given jail terms.
